title: ContextBias: Controlled Evaluation of Bias Persistence Under Context Shift in Text-to-Image Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.29847v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Text-to-image models learn associations between concepts - in the case of this paper, people's professions, which we refer to as roles - and visual attributes. These associations can underpin many observed forms of stereotypical bias. A key open question in this area is whether these associations are stable or change when visual representations of people in professional roles are placed in different prompted contexts. We introduce ContextBias, a controlled evaluation framework, and ContextBench, a benchmark spanning 92 roles and 1,656 semantically controlled prompts, designed to isolate the effect of contextual variation on role-linked visual representations. Evaluating four state-of-the-art models on 66,240 generated images, we find that placing a role in a semantically unrelated context does not suppress role-linked attributes; instead, cross-role attribute concentration increases (pooled BI $+0.047$). translated_title: ContextBias：文生图模型中语境转移下偏见持续性的受控评估
translated_abstract: 文生图模型会学习概念之间的关联——在本文中指的是人们的职业（我们称之为“角色”）与视觉属性之间的关联。这些关联可能构成许多已观察到的刻板印象偏见的基础。该领域的一个关键开放问题是：当处于职业角色中的人物的视觉表征被置于不同的提示语境中时，这些关联是保持稳定还是会发生变化。我们提出了ContextBias这一受控评估框架，以及ContextBench这一涵盖92个角色和1,656个语义受控提示的基准，旨在隔离语境变化对与角色相关联的视觉表征的影响。通过在66,240张生成图像上对四个最先进的模型进行评估，我们发现将一个角色置于语义无关的语境中并不会抑制与角色相关联的属性；相反，跨角色的属性集中度反而增加（合并BI +0.047）。人口统计学线索、特征……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出ContextBias受控评估框架与ContextBench基准（涵盖92个角色、1,656个语义受控提示），通过评估四个最先进模型生成的66,240张图像，发现将职业角色置于语义无关的语境中不仅不会抑制文生图模型中的角色关联属性，反而会使跨角色属性集中度增加，表明偏见在语境转移下持续存在。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ContextBias, a controlled evaluation framework with the ContextBench benchmark (92 roles and 1,656 semantically controlled prompts), and shows through evaluating 66,240 generated images from four state-of-the-art models that placing roles in semantically unrelated contexts does not suppress role-linked attributes in text-to-image models but instead increases cross-role attribute concentration, indicating that bias persists under context shift.
